name: New York
intro: Skyscrapers, Central Park, world-famous museums and the Statue of Liberty. Manhattan is a grid that's easy to walk, and the subway runs all night.

transit.card: OMNY: tap a contactless card or phone
transit.note: The subway runs 24 hours; fares cap after 12 rides in 7 days per card.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Midtown & Times Square
areas.blurb: Times Square, Grand Central and the big viewpoints.

areas.name: Central Park & Museum Mile
areas.blurb: The park, the Met and the Natural History Museum.

areas.name: Lower Manhattan & the harbour
areas.blurb: Statue of Liberty ferries, the 9/11 Memorial and Wall Street.

areas.name: Brooklyn Bridge & DUMBO
areas.blurb: The bridge walk and the waterfront park.

areas.name: Chelsea & High Line
areas.blurb: The elevated park, Chelsea Market and Hudson Yards.

areas.name: Greenwich Village & SoHo
areas.blurb: Washington Square, small streets and old New York.

pois.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
pois.why: The copper statue (93 m with its pedestal), plus the Ellis Island immigration museum, by ferry from Battery Park.
pois.kid: The statue's index finger is 2.4 m long.
pois.tip: Buy only from the official ferry seller; pedestal and crown tickets sell out first. Allow airport-style security.

pois.name: Battery Park
pois.why: The waterfront park at Manhattan's tip, where the Liberty ferries leave.
pois.kid: Ride the SeaGlass carousel shaped like fish.

pois.name: Staten Island Ferry
pois.why: A free 25-minute ferry that passes close to the Statue of Liberty.
pois.kid: Stand on the right side going out for the best Statue view.
pois.tip: Ride there and back; you have to get off and walk round to re-board.

pois.name: 9/11 Memorial
pois.why: Two vast square pools where the Twin Towers stood, with the names of the victims.
pois.tip: Free and open daily; a quiet, respectful place.

pois.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
pois.why: Underground museum of the attacks, with original steel and personal stories.
pois.tip: Very moving; not recommended for young children.

pois.name: One World Observatory
pois.why: Views from the 100th floor of the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere.
pois.kid: The lift ride shows New York being built around you.

pois.name: Wall Street & Charging Bull
pois.why: The financial district's narrow canyons and the bronze bull.
pois.tip: The bull is always crowded; go early.

pois.name: Brooklyn Bridge walk
pois.why: The 1883 suspension bridge with a raised wooden walkway and skyline views.
pois.kid: Count the cables fanning out from the stone towers.
pois.tip: Start in Manhattan and walk to Brooklyn early to beat the crowds; keep out of the bike lane.

pois.name: DUMBO viewpoint (Washington Street)
pois.why: The cobbled street that frames the Manhattan Bridge with the Empire State in between.

pois.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park & Jane's Carousel
pois.why: Waterfront park with lawns, playgrounds and a 1922 carousel in a glass box.
pois.kid: Ride the carousel with the Manhattan skyline behind you.

pois.name: Central Park (Bethesda Terrace)
pois.why: The 340-hectare park: Bethesda Fountain, the Mall, rowing boats and playgrounds.
pois.kid: Rent a rowing boat at the Loeb Boathouse in season.

pois.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
pois.why: One of the world's greatest museums: Egyptian temple, armour, Van Gogh and more.
pois.kid: Visit the Temple of Dendur and the knights in the Arms and Armor hall.

pois.name: American Museum of Natural History
pois.why: Dinosaur halls, the blue whale and the space centre.
pois.kid: Stand under the 29 m blue whale in the ocean hall.
pois.tip: Book a timed entry; go straight to the 4th-floor dinosaurs.

pois.name: Central Park Zoo
pois.why: A small zoo with sea lions, penguins and snow leopards.

pois.name: Belvedere Castle
pois.why: A little stone castle with a view over Turtle Pond.

pois.name: Guggenheim Museum
pois.why: Modern art in Frank Lloyd Wright's spiral building.
pois.kid: Walk the spiral ramp all the way down.

pois.name: Times Square
pois.why: The crossroads of giant screens, best after dark.
pois.kid: Count how many giant screens you can see at once from the red steps.
pois.tip: Watch your bags; costumed characters expect a tip for photos.

pois.name: Top of the Rock
pois.why: Open-air decks with the best view of the Empire State Building and Central Park.
pois.tip: Sunset slots cost more and sell out.

pois.name: Empire State Building
pois.why: The 1931 Art Deco skyscraper with an open-air 86th-floor deck.

pois.name: Grand Central Terminal
pois.why: A grand railway hall with a star-painted ceiling.
pois.kid: Try the Whispering Gallery: whisper into a corner and your friend hears you across the arch.

pois.name: Public Library & Bryant Park
pois.why: The marble library with its stone lions and grand reading room, and the park behind.
pois.kid: Say hello to the lions, named Patience and Fortitude.

pois.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
pois.why: A neo-Gothic cathedral on Fifth Avenue.

pois.name: MoMA
pois.why: Modern art: Van Gogh's Starry Night, Monet's water lilies and Warhol.
pois.kid: Find Starry Night and count the swirls.

pois.name: Intrepid Museum
pois.why: An aircraft carrier turned museum, with jets, a submarine and a space shuttle.
pois.kid: Climb into the submarine and see the space shuttle Enterprise.

pois.name: High Line
pois.why: A park on an old elevated railway, from the Meatpacking District to Hudson Yards.
pois.tip: Lifts at several entrances make it step-free.

pois.name: Chelsea Market
pois.why: An old biscuit factory turned food hall, right under the High Line.
pois.kid: The Oreo was invented in this building.

pois.name: Little Island
pois.why: A park on tulip-shaped pillars in the Hudson River.
pois.tip: Free; timed entry passes may be needed on busy afternoons.

pois.name: Edge observation deck
pois.why: An outdoor sky deck with a glass floor at Hudson Yards.

pois.name: Washington Square Park
pois.why: The arch, fountain and street performers of Greenwich Village.
pois.kid: Watch the street performers around the fountain.

pois.name: SoHo cast-iron streets
pois.why: Shopping streets lined with 19th-century cast-iron buildings.

pois.name: Chinatown dumplings
pois.why: Mott and Doyers Streets for cheap dumplings and noodles.

pois.name: Katz's Delicatessen
pois.why: The 1888 deli famous for hot pastrami sandwiches.
pois.tip: Keep the ticket you get at the door; you pay with it on the way out.

pois.name: Time Out Market (DUMBO)
pois.why: A food hall in an old warehouse with a rooftop view of the bridges.

pois.name: Urbanspace Vanderbilt
pois.why: A food hall next to Grand Central with many quick counters.

pois.name: Plaza Food Hall
pois.why: A food hall under the Plaza Hotel, by the south-east corner of Central Park.

pois.name: Stone Street
pois.why: A cobbled 17th-century lane of restaurants with outdoor tables.

dayTrips.name: Coney Island
dayTrips.from: Subway D, F, N or Q to Coney Island–Stillwell Av
dayTrips.why: The seaside boardwalk with rides, the beach and the New York Aquarium.
highlights: Luna Park rides and the Cyclone coaster
dayTrips.tip: Rides open from spring to early autumn.

dayTrips.name: Bronx Zoo & Botanical Garden
dayTrips.from: Subway 2 or 5 to West Farms Sq, or Metro-North to Botanical Garden
dayTrips.why: One of the world's biggest city zoos, next to a huge botanical garden.

dayTrips.name: Cold Spring (Hudson Valley)
dayTrips.from: Metro-North Hudson line from Grand Central
dayTrips.why: A riverside village with antique shops and hiking trails above the Hudson.
dayTrips.tip: The Breakneck Ridge trail is steep: choose an easier path with kids.

dayTrips.name: Philadelphia
dayTrips.from: Amtrak or NJ Transit from Penn Station
dayTrips.why: America's first capital: the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall and the Rocky steps.
dayTrips.tip: Independence Hall needs free timed tickets.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Tap a contactless bank card or phone at the subway gate (OMNY). Each person needs their own card or phone. Children under 44 inches (112 cm) ride free with a paying adult.

tips.title: Walking the grid
tips.text: Avenues run north–south, streets east–west. Twenty short street blocks are about 1.6 km; avenue blocks are much longer.

tips.title: Money
tips.text: Sales tax is added at the till. Tip 18–20% at sit-down restaurants and about $1–2 per drink at bars.

tips.title: Museums
tips.text: The Met and Natural History Museum have timed tickets. Many museums have free or pay-what-you-wish evenings for locals only; check each site.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: The city is busy but generally safe in tourist areas. Keep phones out of reach on subway platforms. Emergency number: 911.
